definitions.explanation: The practice of attaching the honorific suffix さん to a person's name when addressing or referring to them. Indicates a basic level of politeness and respect.

examples.japanese: ⟦{職場|しょくば}→職場：04164_shokuba⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧さん{付|づ}け⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{基本|きほん}→基本：00226_kihon⟧だ。
examples.english: In the workplace, using -san is the norm.

examples.japanese: うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧さん{付|づ}け⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{呼|よ}び{合|あ}う。
examples.english: At our company, we address each other with -san.

examples.japanese: ⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{部下|ぶか}→部下：06453_buka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧さん{付|づ}け⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{呼|よ}ぶ→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧ようにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: More companies are adopting the practice of addressing both superiors and subordinates with -san.

notes:
The word {付|づ}け means 'attaching' or 'affixing,' so さん{付|づ}け literally means 'attaching さん.' This pattern is productive: ちゃん{付|づ}け (using -chan), ⟦くん→くれる：00724_kureru⟧{付|づ}け (using -kun), ⟦{様|さま}→様：01549_sama⟧{付|づ}け (using -sama) all follow the same structure. In many Japanese workplaces, there has been a trend toward さん{付|づ}け as a way to create a more egalitarian atmosphere, replacing ⟦{役職|やくしょく}→役職：05514_yakushoku⟧⟦{呼|よ}び→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧ (addressing by job title).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- さん{付|づ}け⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{呼|よ}ぶ→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧: to address with -san
- さん{付|づ}け⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{基本|きほん}→基本：00226_kihon⟧: -san is the standard
- さん{付|づ}け⟦ルール→ルール：00354_ruuru⟧: -san rule (company policy)

RELATED WORDS:
- ちゃん{付|づ}け: using -chan — more familiar, for children or close relationships
- ⟦くん→くれる：00724_kureru⟧{付|づ}け: using -kun — used toward male peers or subordinates
- ⟦{呼|よ}び{捨|す}て→呼び捨て：15868_yobisute⟧: calling someone by name without an honorific — considered rude unless the relationship is very close
